subject: English 1st Paper (English For Today)
topic: Writing Dialogues (Question No. 13: প্রাত্যহিক জীবনের বাস্তব পরিস্থিতি নিয়ে কথোপকথন রচনা)
book: Original practice; Class 8 Model Test format

items.text: 13. Suppose you are Rafi and your friend is Nila. Make a dialogue between you and your friend about the importance of learning English.
items.explanation:
Sample dialogue:
Rafi: Why are you practising English every day?
Nila: I want to communicate with more people and read useful books.
Rafi: Is memorising words enough?
Nila: No. We should practise listening, speaking, reading and writing.
Rafi: How can we improve together?
Nila: Let us read a short article and discuss it in English each week.
Rafi: Shall we practise pronunciation as well?
Nila: Yes, and we can ask our teacher when we are unsure.
Rafi: I will bring an article tomorrow.
Nila: Great. Let us choose a topic we both enjoy.
items.page: Original practice; model test Q13 format.

items.text: 13. Suppose you are Rafi and your friend is Nila. Make a dialogue between you and your friend about the benefits of reading books.
items.explanation:
Sample dialogue:
Rafi: What are you reading from the library?
Nila: A collection of stories about different places.
Rafi: Why do you enjoy reading?
Nila: It develops my imagination and introduces new ideas.
Rafi: How do you find time?
Nila: I read a few pages after finishing my homework.
Rafi: Can you recommend a book for me?
Nila: Ask the librarian for an age-appropriate suggestion.
Rafi: May I borrow yours afterwards?
Nila: Yes, once I return it to the library.
items.page: Original practice; model test Q13 format.

items.text: 13. Suppose you are Rafi and your friend is Nila. Make a dialogue between you and your friend about planting and caring for trees.
items.explanation:
Sample dialogue:
Rafi: Shall we plant a tree at school?
Nila: Yes, but we should first ask the teacher where it is suitable.
Rafi: What kind of tree should we choose?
Nila: A local expert can suggest a species suited to the site.
Rafi: Is planting enough?
Nila: No. We must also water and protect the young tree.
Rafi: Who will look after the sapling during holidays?
Nila: We should arrange an adult-supervised schedule.
Rafi: Let us check on it regularly.
Nila: Agreed. A healthy tree needs long-term care.
items.page: Original practice; model test Q13 format.

items.text: 13. Suppose you are Rafi and your friend is Nila. Make a dialogue between you and your friend about keeping the classroom clean.
items.explanation:
Sample dialogue:
Rafi: Why are you carrying a rubbish bag?
Nila: Our classroom needs cleaning after the art activity.
Rafi: Can I help?
Nila: Certainly. Please collect the paper scraps from the desks.
Rafi: Where should we put them?
Nila: In the appropriate bin, and we should wash our hands afterwards.
Rafi: Shall we organise the supplies too?
Nila: Yes, and we should return them to their proper places.
Rafi: The room looks much better now.
Nila: It will stay that way if everyone helps.
items.page: Original practice; model test Q13 format.

items.text: 13. Suppose you are Rafi and your friend is Nila. Make a dialogue between you and your friend about preparing for an examination.
items.explanation:
Sample dialogue:
Rafi: How are you preparing for the examination?
Nila: I made a timetable for each subject.
Rafi: Do you study without a break?
Nila: No. I take short breaks and sleep properly.
Rafi: What do you do with difficult questions?
Nila: I try them first and then ask my teacher for help.
Rafi: Will you revise with me tomorrow?
Nila: Yes. We can explain difficult ideas to each other.
Rafi: Let us start with mathematics.
Nila: Good idea. We can check our answers afterwards.
items.page: Original practice; model test Q13 format.

items.text: 13. Suppose you are Rafi and your friend is Nila. Make a dialogue between you and your friend about the value of punctuality.
items.explanation:
Sample dialogue:
Rafi: Why do you leave home so early?
Nila: I want enough time to reach school safely.
Rafi: Does punctuality matter outside school?
Nila: Yes. It shows respect for other people’s time.
Rafi: What if an unexpected delay occurs?
Nila: We should inform the person waiting as soon as possible.
Rafi: How do you remember the time?
Nila: I prepare my bag the night before and set a reminder.
Rafi: I will try that too.
Nila: It may make the morning less hurried.
items.page: Original practice; model test Q13 format.

items.text: 13. Suppose you are Rafi and your friend is Nila. Make a dialogue between you and your friend about saving water at home.
items.explanation:
Sample dialogue:
Rafi: The tap is dripping again. What should we do?
Nila: Let us tell an adult so it can be repaired.
Rafi: Can small leaks waste water?
Nila: Yes. A steady drip can add up over time.
Rafi: How else can we save water?
Nila: We can turn taps off properly and use only what we need.
Rafi: Should we tell everyone about the leak?
Nila: Let us inform the person responsible for repairs first.
Rafi: I will check that the other taps are closed.
Nila: Thank you. Small habits can make a difference.
items.page: Original practice; model test Q13 format.

items.text: 13. Suppose you are Rafi and your friend is Nila. Make a dialogue between you and your friend about a school library.
items.explanation:
Sample dialogue:
Rafi: Have you visited the new school library?
Nila: Yes. It has storybooks, reference books and a quiet reading area.
Rafi: How can I borrow a book?
Nila: Ask the librarian about the borrowing rules and due date.
Rafi: Why should we return books on time?
Nila: Other readers may be waiting to use them.
Rafi: Can we study there together?
Nila: Yes, if we speak quietly and follow the library rules.
Rafi: I will ask the librarian for a card.
Nila: Then we can choose our books.
items.page: Original practice; model test Q13 format.

items.text: 13. Suppose you are Rafi and your friend is Nila. Make a dialogue between you and your friend about regular physical exercise.
items.explanation:
Sample dialogue:
Rafi: Why do you walk in the afternoon?
Nila: It helps me stay active and refreshed.
Rafi: Must everyone follow the same routine?
Nila: No. Activities should suit a person’s health and ability.
Rafi: What about students with health concerns?
Nila: They should ask a qualified health professional for suitable advice.
Rafi: Shall we invite another friend on our walk?
Nila: Yes, if the route and time are suitable for everyone.
Rafi: I will bring a water bottle.
Nila: Good. We can take breaks when needed.
items.page: Original practice; model test Q13 format.

items.text: 13. Suppose you are Rafi and your friend is Nila. Make a dialogue between you and your friend about a rainy day journey.
items.explanation:
Sample dialogue:
Rafi: The rain is heavy. Should we leave now?
Nila: Let us wait in a safe place until it becomes lighter.
Rafi: The road near the canal may be flooded.
Nila: Then we should avoid it and ask an adult about a safer route.
Rafi: Do you have an umbrella?
Nila: Yes, and we can share it when it is safe to walk.
Rafi: What if the water rises before we leave?
Nila: We should remain in a safe place and follow official guidance.
Rafi: I will let my family know where we are.
Nila: That is sensible. Let us avoid rushing.
items.page: Original practice; model test Q13 format.

items.text: 13. Suppose you are Rafi and your friend is Nila. Make a dialogue between you and your friend about a school sports day.
items.explanation:
Sample dialogue:
Rafi: Are you taking part in sports day?
Nila: Yes. I will run in a short race.
Rafi: How are you preparing?
Nila: I practise with my teacher and warm up before running.
Rafi: What happens if you do not win?
Nila: I will congratulate the winners and learn from the experience.
Rafi: Will you cheer for the other runners too?
Nila: Of course. Everyone deserves encouragement.
Rafi: We should follow the officials’ instructions.
Nila: Yes. Safety and fairness matter more than winning.
items.page: Original practice; model test Q13 format.

items.text: 13. Suppose you are Rafi and your friend is Nila. Make a dialogue between you and your friend about the importance of honesty.
items.explanation:
Sample dialogue:
Rafi: I found extra change after buying a notebook.
Nila: What will you do with it?
Rafi: I will return to the shop and explain the mistake.
Nila: Why is that important?
Rafi: The extra money belongs to the shopkeeper, not to me.
Nila: I agree. Honesty helps people trust one another.
Rafi: Will you come with me to the shop?
Nila: Certainly. We can explain the situation politely.
Rafi: I hope the shopkeeper remembers the purchase.
Nila: Let us take the receipt if you have it.
items.page: Original practice; model test Q13 format.

items.text: 13. Suppose you are Rafi and your friend is Nila. Make a dialogue between you and your friend about using the internet responsibly.
items.explanation:
Sample dialogue:
Rafi: Can I believe everything I read online?
Nila: No. Check important information against reliable sources.
Rafi: Should I share my password with a friend?
Nila: No. Keep passwords private and ask a trusted adult for help.
Rafi: What if someone sends a troubling message?
Nila: Do not reply; tell a trusted adult and use the appropriate report feature.
Rafi: Can we check the source together?
Nila: Yes. We can compare it with trusted information.
Rafi: I will ask a teacher about this claim.
Nila: Good. It is wise to pause before sharing.
items.page: Original practice; model test Q13 format.

items.text: 13. Suppose you are Rafi and your friend is Nila. Make a dialogue between you and your friend about visiting a book fair.
items.explanation:
Sample dialogue:
Rafi: Would you like to visit the book fair?
Nila: Yes. I want to compare some science and storybooks.
Rafi: Have you decided how much to spend?
Nila: I have a small budget and will check prices first.
Rafi: What if a book costs too much?
Nila: I can ask whether the library has a copy to borrow.
Rafi: Shall we make a list before going?
Nila: Yes. It will help us stay within our budget.
Rafi: I also want to attend a reading.
Nila: Let us check the event schedule first.
items.page: Original practice; model test Q13 format.

items.text: 13. Suppose you are Rafi and your friend is Nila. Make a dialogue between you and your friend about a healthy breakfast.
items.explanation:
Sample dialogue:
Rafi: Why do you eat breakfast before school?
Nila: It gives me a chance to start the day with food and energy.
Rafi: What do you usually eat?
Nila: I choose from foods available at home, such as bread, eggs or fruit.
Rafi: Should everyone eat the same meal?
Nila: No. Needs and choices vary, and a balanced diet matters.
Rafi: Can we bring water to school too?
Nila: Yes, in a clean bottle filled with safe drinking water.
Rafi: I will plan my breakfast tonight.
Nila: That may make the morning easier.
items.page: Original practice; model test Q13 format.

items.text: 13. Suppose you are Rafi and your friend is Nila. Make a dialogue between you and your friend about keeping a school garden.
items.explanation:
Sample dialogue:
Rafi: The garden soil looks dry. Shall we water it?
Nila: Yes, after our teacher checks what the plants need.
Rafi: Who will care for it during the week?
Nila: Our group can prepare a schedule.
Rafi: Can we plant more seeds?
Nila: Let us first check whether there is enough suitable space.
Rafi: Shall we record the plants’ growth?
Nila: Yes. We can note the date and changes in a notebook.
Rafi: I will speak to the teacher today.
Nila: Then we can begin with an agreed plan.
items.page: Original practice; model test Q13 format.

items.text: 13. Suppose you are Rafi and your friend is Nila. Make a dialogue between you and your friend about helping a new classmate.
items.explanation:
Sample dialogue:
Rafi: The new student is sitting alone.
Nila: Let us invite her to join our group.
Rafi: What can we show her first?
Nila: We can explain the timetable and show her the library.
Rafi: What if she prefers some quiet time?
Nila: We should respect that and let her know we are available.
Rafi: Would you introduce yourself first?
Nila: Yes. I will ask whether she would like company.
Rafi: We can answer her questions about school.
Nila: That may help her settle in comfortably.
items.page: Original practice; model test Q13 format.

items.text: 13. Suppose you are Rafi and your friend is Nila. Make a dialogue between you and your friend about road safety.
items.explanation:
Sample dialogue:
Rafi: How do you cross this busy road?
Nila: I use the designated crossing when it is safe.
Rafi: Should we run between vehicles?
Nila: No. We should wait, look carefully and follow traffic signals.
Rafi: Can younger children cross alone?
Nila: They should follow their family’s guidance and seek adult help when needed.
Rafi: What should we do near the crossing?
Nila: Pay attention to traffic and avoid distractions.
Rafi: Let us wait for the signal.
Nila: Yes. We should never hurry into the road.
items.page: Original practice; model test Q13 format.

items.text: 13. Suppose you are Rafi and your friend is Nila. Make a dialogue between you and your friend about a visit to a museum.
items.explanation:
Sample dialogue:
Rafi: What did you enjoy at the museum?
Nila: I liked the displays about local history.
Rafi: How did you learn about the objects?
Nila: I read the labels and listened to the guide.
Rafi: Could you touch the exhibits?
Nila: Only if the museum specifically allowed it.
Rafi: Did you take notes during the visit?
Nila: Yes. They will help with my report.
Rafi: Can I see the guidebook later?
Nila: Certainly. We can discuss what we learned.
items.page: Original practice; model test Q13 format.

items.text: 13. Suppose you are Rafi and your friend is Nila. Make a dialogue between you and your friend about the importance of good manners.
items.explanation:
Sample dialogue:
Rafi: Why did you thank the bus conductor?
Nila: He helped me find the correct stop.
Rafi: Are good manners only about saying thank you?
Nila: No. They also include listening and treating others respectfully.
Rafi: What if we make a mistake?
Nila: We can apologise sincerely and try to put it right.
Rafi: Does listening show respect too?
Nila: Yes. It shows that we value another person’s ideas.
Rafi: I will remember to wait my turn.
Nila: That makes conversations pleasant for everyone.
items.page: Original practice; model test Q13 format.

items.text: 13. Suppose you are Rafi and your friend is Nila. Make a dialogue between you and your friend about preparing for a debate.
items.explanation:
Sample dialogue:
Rafi: How are you preparing for the debate?
Nila: I am collecting reliable evidence for our team’s argument.
Rafi: Should we ignore the other team’s points?
Nila: No. We should listen and respond respectfully.
Rafi: What will you practise next?
Nila: I will explain my main point within the time limit.
Rafi: Shall we practise a response to questions?
Nila: Yes. We can take turns asking each other questions.
Rafi: I will bring my notes.
Nila: I will check the sources we used.
items.page: Original practice; model test Q13 format.

items.text: 13. Suppose you are Rafi and your friend is Nila. Make a dialogue between you and your friend about reducing plastic waste.
items.explanation:
Sample dialogue:
Rafi: Our picnic produced many wrappers.
Nila: Next time we can carry reusable containers where practical.
Rafi: What should we do with this waste?
Nila: Sort and dispose of it according to local rules.
Rafi: Can we pick up every object ourselves?
Nila: No. Leave sharp or hazardous items to responsible adults.
Rafi: Can our class discuss reducing waste?
Nila: Yes. We can suggest practical changes to the teacher.
Rafi: Let us start with our own lunches.
Nila: That is a useful first step.
items.page: Original practice; model test Q13 format.

items.text: 13. Suppose you are Rafi and your friend is Nila. Make a dialogue between you and your friend about the uses of a dictionary.
items.explanation:
Sample dialogue:
Rafi: What are you looking up?
Nila: A word I found in a story.
Rafi: The dictionary gives several meanings.
Nila: We need the meaning that fits the sentence.
Rafi: Should I record it?
Nila: Yes. Write an example sentence to help you remember.
Rafi: What if I still cannot understand the word?
Nila: Ask your teacher or read another example.
Rafi: I will try it in a sentence.
Nila: Good. Context often makes the meaning clearer.
items.page: Original practice; model test Q13 format.

items.text: 13. Suppose you are Rafi and your friend is Nila. Make a dialogue between you and your friend about a school science fair.
items.explanation:
Sample dialogue:
Rafi: What is your science fair project about?
Nila: Our group is observing how seedlings grow in different light.
Rafi: How will you record the results?
Nila: We will measure them and write observations each day.
Rafi: What if the results surprise you?
Nila: We will report them honestly and discuss possible reasons.
Rafi: Who will explain the project to visitors?
Nila: We will take turns so everyone can participate.
Rafi: Let us prepare for questions.
Nila: Yes, but we should admit what we do not know.
items.page: Original practice; model test Q13 format.

items.text: 13. Suppose you are Rafi and your friend is Nila. Make a dialogue between you and your friend about sharing household work.
items.explanation:
Sample dialogue:
Rafi: Why are you helping in the kitchen?
Nila: Everyone in the family can share suitable tasks.
Rafi: What can you do safely?
Nila: I can wash vegetables and set the table.
Rafi: Who handles the hot stove?
Nila: An adult does, and I follow their guidance.
Rafi: Can I help set the table?
Nila: Certainly. Please carry the unbreakable plates.
Rafi: What should I do afterwards?
Nila: Wash your hands and put away the clean utensils.
items.page: Original practice; model test Q13 format.

items.text: 13. Suppose you are Rafi and your friend is Nila. Make a dialogue between you and your friend about choosing a future career.
items.explanation:
Sample dialogue:
Rafi: What would you like to do in the future?
Nila: I am interested in becoming a teacher.
Rafi: Why does that appeal to you?
Nila: I enjoy explaining ideas and helping others learn.
Rafi: What can you do now?
Nila: I can study carefully, practise communication and explore the profession.
Rafi: Could you speak with a teacher about the career?
Nila: Yes. I would like to learn about the training required.
Rafi: Interests can change as we grow.
Nila: That is true. I will keep exploring.
items.page: Original practice; model test Q13 format.

items.text: 13. Suppose you are Rafi and your friend is Nila. Make a dialogue between you and your friend about a village market.
items.explanation:
Sample dialogue:
Rafi: What do people buy at the village market?
Nila: They buy vegetables, fish, household items and many other things.
Rafi: Why is it important to the community?
Nila: It brings buyers and sellers together and supports livelihoods.
Rafi: What should visitors remember?
Nila: They should keep the area clean and treat sellers respectfully.
Rafi: When is the market busiest?
Nila: It may be busiest on the main market day.
Rafi: Shall we visit with our families?
Nila: Yes. We can observe how it serves the area.
items.page: Original practice; model test Q13 format.

items.text: 13. Suppose you are Rafi and your friend is Nila. Make a dialogue between you and your friend about a train journey.
items.explanation:
Sample dialogue:
Rafi: How did you prepare for your train journey?
Nila: We checked the schedule and reached the station early.
Rafi: What did you see from the window?
Nila: I saw fields, rivers and small settlements.
Rafi: Did you move around while the train was moving?
Nila: No. We followed the railway’s safety instructions.
Rafi: Did you keep your ticket safely?
Nila: Yes. I also followed the staff’s instructions.
Rafi: I would enjoy a journey like that.
Nila: Planning ahead can make travel more comfortable.
items.page: Original practice; model test Q13 format.

items.text: 13. Suppose you are Rafi and your friend is Nila. Make a dialogue between you and your friend about a school picnic.
items.explanation:
Sample dialogue:
Rafi: Where will your class have its picnic?
Nila: At a park chosen by our teachers.
Rafi: What should we bring?
Nila: Water, suitable food and anything listed in the school notice.
Rafi: How will we keep the park clean?
Nila: We will collect our waste and use the proper bins.
Rafi: Will the teachers explain the safety rules?
Nila: Yes, before we leave and again at the park.
Rafi: I will read the notice carefully.
Nila: I will do the same and arrive on time.
items.page: Original practice; model test Q13 format.

items.text: 13. Suppose you are Rafi and your friend is Nila. Make a dialogue between you and your friend about the importance of sleep.
items.explanation:
Sample dialogue:
Rafi: Why are you turning off your phone so early?
Nila: I want enough time to sleep before school.
Rafi: Does sleep help learning?
Nila: Rest supports attention and general well-being.
Rafi: What if someone regularly cannot sleep well?
Nila: They should speak with a trusted adult or health professional.
Rafi: Do you keep a regular bedtime?
Nila: I try to follow a consistent routine.
Rafi: I will put my book away soon.
Nila: Good. Tomorrow will be a busy day.
items.page: Original practice; model test Q13 format.

items.text: 13. Suppose you are Rafi and your friend is Nila. Make a dialogue between you and your friend about visiting a sick friend.
items.explanation:
Sample dialogue:
Rafi: Our friend has been absent because she is ill.
Nila: Shall we ask her family whether a visit is suitable?
Rafi: Yes. We should not visit without checking.
Nila: Can we help with schoolwork?
Rafi: We can share the notes when she feels ready.
Nila: That sounds like a thoughtful plan.
Rafi: Shall we send a kind message first?
Nila: Yes, and we can ask her family what is helpful.
Rafi: We should respect her need for rest.
Nila: Absolutely. Her recovery comes first.
items.page: Original practice; model test Q13 format.

items.text: 13. Suppose you are Rafi and your friend is Nila. Make a dialogue between you and your friend about keeping food safe.
items.explanation:
Sample dialogue:
Rafi: Why are you covering the food?
Nila: It helps protect the food from dust and insects.
Rafi: Should we wash our hands before preparing it?
Nila: Yes, and we should use clean utensils and safe water.
Rafi: Who will handle the hot pan?
Nila: An adult will handle it safely.
Rafi: Where should we store the fruit?
Nila: In a clean place, following the family’s food-safety guidance.
Rafi: I will clean the table.
Nila: Thank you. I will put away the utensils.
items.page: Original practice; model test Q13 format.

items.text: 13. Suppose you are Rafi and your friend is Nila. Make a dialogue between you and your friend about organising a class timetable.
items.explanation:
Sample dialogue:
Rafi: We have several assignments due this week.
Nila: Let us list the deadlines on a calendar.
Rafi: Should we leave the hardest one until the last day?
Nila: No. We can divide it into smaller steps and begin early.
Rafi: Can we include breaks?
Nila: Of course. A realistic schedule needs time for rest.
Rafi: Who will update the calendar?
Nila: We can take turns checking it each evening.
Rafi: Let us include the test date too.
Nila: Yes. That will help us prepare in advance.
items.page: Original practice; model test Q13 format.

items.text: 13. Suppose you are Rafi and your friend is Nila. Make a dialogue between you and your friend about helping during heavy rain.
items.explanation:
Sample dialogue:
Rafi: Heavy rain has flooded the lane near our house.
Nila: We should stay away from floodwater and listen to local advice.
Rafi: Can we help our neighbours?
Nila: We can ask responsible adults what safe help is needed.
Rafi: Should children enter the water to collect things?
Nila: No. Safety and adult guidance must come first.
Rafi: Can we collect supplies for affected families?
Nila: Only with adult coordination and according to local needs.
Rafi: I will ask our teacher how to contribute.
Nila: Good. Organised help is more useful and safer.
items.page: Original practice; model test Q13 format.

items.text: 13. Suppose you are Rafi and your friend is Nila. Make a dialogue between you and your friend about writing a school magazine.
items.explanation:
Sample dialogue:
Rafi: What shall we include in the school magazine?
Nila: We could publish poems, drawings and short reports.
Rafi: How will we select the pieces?
Nila: The editorial team can use clear and fair criteria.
Rafi: Should we check facts before printing?
Nila: Yes. We should also get permission for borrowed material.
Rafi: How can students submit their work?
Nila: The teacher can announce a clear deadline and method.
Rafi: I would like to submit a poem.
Nila: Please do. We will review every submission fairly.
items.page: Original practice; model test Q13 format.

items.text: 13. Suppose you are Rafi and your friend is Nila. Make a dialogue between you and your friend about learning a new skill.
items.explanation:
Sample dialogue:
Rafi: Why are you practising sewing?
Nila: I want to learn how to repair a loose button.
Rafi: Is it difficult?
Nila: At first, but an adult showed me each step.
Rafi: How do you handle the needle?
Nila: Carefully, under supervision, and I put it away afterwards.
Rafi: May I watch your next lesson?
Nila: Yes, if the adult supervising agrees.
Rafi: I would like to practise on spare cloth.
Nila: That is a sensible way to begin.
items.page: Original practice; model test Q13 format.

items.text: 13. Suppose you are Rafi and your friend is Nila. Make a dialogue between you and your friend about the benefits of teamwork.
items.explanation:
Sample dialogue:
Rafi: Our group project has many tasks.
Nila: Let us divide them according to what each person can do.
Rafi: What if someone needs help?
Nila: We can explain the task and support each other.
Rafi: How will we make a decision?
Nila: Everyone should have a chance to share an idea.
Rafi: What should we do if the work is uneven?
Nila: Discuss it kindly and adjust the responsibilities.
Rafi: Let us check our progress tomorrow.
Nila: Agreed. We can make changes together.
items.page: Original practice; model test Q13 format.

items.text: 13. Suppose you are Rafi and your friend is Nila. Make a dialogue between you and your friend about visiting a community clinic.
items.explanation:
Sample dialogue:
Rafi: Why is the community clinic important?
Nila: It can provide local people with basic health services.
Rafi: Can we decide our own treatment from a friend’s advice?
Nila: No. We should consult qualified health workers.
Rafi: How can we help the clinic stay organised?
Nila: Follow its instructions and treat the staff and patients respectfully.
Rafi: What if the clinic is closed?
Nila: An adult can check the available local health services.
Rafi: I will keep the clinic’s hours noted.
Nila: That can help the family plan a visit.
items.page: Original practice; model test Q13 format.

items.text: 13. Suppose you are Rafi and your friend is Nila. Make a dialogue between you and your friend about saving electricity.
items.explanation:
Sample dialogue:
Rafi: Why did you switch off the light?
Nila: No one was using the room.
Rafi: What else can we do?
Nila: Turn off appliances when appropriate and use daylight safely.
Rafi: Will that solve every power problem?
Nila: No, but careful use can reduce unnecessary consumption.
Rafi: Can we remind others without scolding?
Nila: Yes. A polite reminder is more helpful.
Rafi: I will check the fan before leaving.
Nila: And I will check the lights.

items.text: 13. Suppose you are Rafi and your friend is Nila. Make a dialogue between you and your friend about a favourite game.
items.explanation:
Sample dialogue:
Rafi: What game do you enjoy?
Nila: I enjoy badminton with my friends.
Rafi: What makes it enjoyable?
Nila: It needs movement, concentration and cooperation.
Rafi: How do you keep the game fair?
Nila: We follow the rules and respect each other.
Rafi: Shall we play after school?
Nila: Yes, if our homework and the weather allow.
Rafi: We need a safe place to play.
Nila: Let us ask which court is available.

items.text: 13. Suppose you are Rafi and your friend is Nila. Make a dialogue between you and your friend about a school cultural programme.
items.explanation:
Sample dialogue:
Rafi: What are you doing for the cultural programme?
Nila: Our group is preparing a short play.
Rafi: How did you choose the roles?
Nila: We discussed everyone’s interests and available time.
Rafi: What if someone forgets a line?
Nila: We will help one another and continue calmly.
Rafi: When is the next rehearsal?
Nila: Our teacher scheduled it for Thursday.
Rafi: I will read the script beforehand.
Nila: That will help the group use its time well.

items.text: 13. Suppose you are Rafi and your friend is Nila. Make a dialogue between you and your friend about preparing a first aid plan.
items.explanation:
Sample dialogue:
Rafi: What should we do if a classmate is injured?
Nila: Tell a teacher or another responsible adult immediately.
Rafi: Can we give medicine ourselves?
Nila: No. Follow the guidance of qualified adults and school procedures.
Rafi: Why keep emergency contacts available?
Nila: They help adults contact the right people quickly.
Rafi: Where is the school’s first aid kit?
Nila: The teacher can tell us where it is kept.
Rafi: Should we leave an injured student alone?
Nila: No. Stay nearby and seek appropriate adult help.

items.text: 13. Suppose you are Rafi and your friend is Nila. Make a dialogue between you and your friend about visiting a historical place.

Sample dialogue:
Rafi: What did you learn on your visit?
Nila: I learned about the building’s history from the guide.
Rafi: How can we protect such places?
Nila: Follow visitor rules and avoid damaging walls or objects.
Rafi: Can we photograph everything?
Nila: Only where photography is permitted.
Rafi: Can we read more about the site?
Nila: Yes. Let us look for a reliable history book.
Rafi: I will share my notes from the guide.
Nila: Thank you. We can compare what we learned.

items.text: 13. Suppose you are Rafi and your friend is Nila. Make a dialogue between you and your friend about respecting different opinions.
items.explanation:
Sample dialogue:
Rafi: I disagree with your idea for the project.
Nila: That is all right. Please explain your reasons.
Rafi: Can we listen to both plans first?
Nila: Yes, then we can compare their strengths.
Rafi: What if we still disagree?
Nila: We can use a fair decision-making process without personal attacks.
Rafi: Shall we write down both ideas?
Nila: Yes. Then the whole group can consider them.
Rafi: I appreciate your listening.
Nila: I appreciate your explaining your view.

items.text: 13. Suppose you are Rafi and your friend is Nila. Make a dialogue between you and your friend about the importance of keeping promises.

items.text: 13. Suppose you are Rafi and your friend is Nila. Make a dialogue between you and your friend about using time wisely.

items.text: 13. Suppose you are Rafi and your friend is Nila. Make a dialogue between you and your friend about a school tree observation.
